scene: THE TAKE / Jerky Motel / The Beef Run
reference: THE TAKE is Heat. The Motel is a cartel buy that goes wrong. The Beef Run is contraband hauled through mountains.
diagnosis: THE TAKE has one outright doctrine violation — the Counter-Strike line winks directly at the player mid-standoff — and a debrief where a mob boss reacts to a dead civilian like a middle manager reviewing a quarter. The Motel keeps putting mission objectives in mouths ('Buy. Leave. No speeches.') and then has two different characters recite the same rulebook phrase at each other. Across all three, the Prospect answers everything in one flat word: 'Yes.' 'Why?' 'Understood.' He is the player's mouth and right now he has no tongue.

lines.current: Good thing about all that Counter-Strike I've been playing.
lines.why: CUT OR REWRITE — this is the doctrine violation. It names a real game, acknowledges the player, and tells the audience the scene is a joke at the exact moment the scene has to be a bank robbery. Everything the tone doc protects dies on this line.
lines.house: [cut it — or, if the beat is needed] Everything's slower than I thought it'd be. Why is everything so slow.
lines.tarantino: Nobody tells you it's quiet. You think it's going to be loud, and it's this. It's a man breathing through a mask and a woman's shoe squeaking on a floor.
lines.mcdonagh: It's not like I thought. In me head there was music. There's no music. There's just this fella breathin' on me.
lines.houser: Turns out the whole thing is admin. Stand here, count that, watch the door. Nobody mentions the admin.
lines.coen: Huh. It's a lot slower than you'd think. That's the part nobody mentions.

lines.current: Hey guys, what's going on?
lines.why: A YouTube-intro catchphrase dropped into a heist debrief. The Shubenator wandering in is a world joke, which the doctrine allows — but he has to wander in playing his own situation straight, not doing a bit at the camera.
lines.house: Hey. Hey — is this a bad time? This feels like a bad time.
lines.tarantino: Hey. Sorry. Am I early? Because Snow said four, and it's four, but everybody's got a face on, so I'm getting the sense four was wrong.
lines.mcdonagh: Howya. Am I interruptin'? I am, amn't I. I'll come back. I'll not come back, I'll just stand here quietly.
lines.houser: Hey, guys. Big energy in here. Is this a debrief? Should I not be at the debrief? Nobody adds me to things.
lines.coen: Hey there. Everything all right? Because it doesn't seem all right, and I'd just as soon come back later.

lines.current: Armor is on. Magazines are full. I heard the plan.
lines.why: A UI status readout wearing dialogue. Nobody inventories themselves out loud. Give it the physical detail of a man about to do this for the first time.
lines.house: I'm on. Vest is on, mags are full, and my hands won't stop.
lines.tarantino: I'm ready. I've been ready for about forty minutes, which I'm now realising is a completely different thing from being ready.
lines.mcdonagh: I'm set. Vest, mags, the whole lot. And I've been sick twice, but I'm set.
lines.houser: Vest on, mags full, plan understood. And I want it on record I have never done anything like this and I am doing it anyway.
lines.coen: I'm ready. Everything's on, everything's full. I heard the plan twice. I'd hear it a third time if there was time.

lines.current: Down. Face on the floor, hands where I can see them.
lines.why: Robbery-command boilerplate. This is the kid's first time raising his voice at civilians — it should be too loud, badly pitched, and frightening because of that.
lines.house: DOWN. On the floor, face down, hands out. Nobody makes me say it twice.
lines.tarantino: Everybody down. Face down, hands flat, and look at the carpet. Look at the carpet and count. That's the whole job — you count, I count, we all go home.
lines.mcdonagh: Down! Get down! Faces down, hands out, and not one of yiz look at me. I mean it. Don't look at me.
lines.houser: On the floor. Face down, hands out, phones stay in the pocket. This is a robbery, not a live event.
lines.coen: Everybody down on the floor, please. Face down. Hands out where I can see them. Please.

lines.current: Mask is down. I can see fine.
lines.why: Pure status filler. There is a much better line hiding in what a mask actually does to a man's head.
lines.house: Mask's down. I can't hear right with this thing on.
lines.tarantino: Mask's down. And here's a thing nobody mentions — you can hear yourself. That's all you can hear. Just you, in there, breathing.
lines.mcdonagh: Mask's on. I can see grand. I can hear me own heart, which is new.
lines.houser: Mask down. Visibility's fine. Everything else about me is a work in progress.
lines.coen: Mask's down. I can see okay. It's warm in here, is all.

lines.current: Stop right there. Hands where I can see them.
lines.why: The most generic guard bark in the medium. This man is fifty-eight, unarmed by policy, and about to make the worst decision of his life.
lines.house: Hey. HEY. Don't — I'm not supposed to — just stop.
lines.tarantino: Stop. Stop right there. I want you to know I'm not supposed to engage. There's a card in my wallet that says I'm not supposed to engage. And here I am.
lines.mcdonagh: Stop where you are! Hands up! I've a card in me wallet says I'm not to do this, and here I am doin' it.
lines.houser: Stop. Hands up. I earn eleven dollars an hour and I am about to earn every one of them.
lines.coen: Hold it right there. Hands up, please. I'd rather not — let's just, let's not have this go the other way.

lines.current: First one, and you already know the answer. Somebody who came in to cash a cheque did not walk back out. That follows this family around for years.
lines.why: The content is right and the temperature is wrong. Lou is being an HR memo about a dead civilian. He should be furious in the specific way a man is furious about money and heat, which is uglier than being furious about the death.
lines.house: Somebody came in to cash a cheque and went home in a bag. That is not a robbery any more, kid. That's a murder with a bank attached, and it sits on this family for twenty years.
lines.tarantino: You know what you did. A woman came in on her lunch break to cash a cheque, and she is not going back to work. Now here's the part you're not thinking about. Nobody looks for money. Everybody looks for a body. You didn't rob a bank today. You made a bank into a place where somebody died, and that has a memory on it like nothing else in this business.
lines.mcdonagh: Some poor woman came in to cash a cheque and went out under a sheet. D'you know what that is? That's twenty years. That's twenty years of every guard in this state havin' a photo of her on a wall and your name under it.
lines.houser: A customer came in to cash a cheque and left in a bag. Do you understand what you've done to the risk profile of this entire organization? You have converted a property crime into a homicide, and homicide has no statute of limitations and no sense of humour.
lines.coen: Somebody came in to cash a cheque. And she didn't go home. That's the thing that stays. The money goes. That stays.

lines.current: Then it was a good day. Nobody hurt, everything counted, and tomorrow it is a paragraph nobody reads. Well done, kid.
lines.why: 'Well done, kid' is a little-league coach. Lou's approval should feel like being handed something heavy you cannot put down.
lines.house: Then it was a good day. Nobody bleeding, everything counted, and by Thursday it's a paragraph nobody reads. You did that. Now go home before you start liking it.
lines.tarantino: Then it was a good day. Nobody hurt, every number matched, and by Thursday it's a paragraph on page eleven that nobody finishes. You know how rare that is? I've been doing this forty years and I can count the clean ones on one hand. Go home. Sleep badly. That part never stops.
lines.mcdonagh: Then it was a good day. Nobody hurt, everythin' counted, and by Thursday it's a paragraph no one reads. Good lad. Now go home and don't be gettin' fond of it.
lines.houser: Then that's a good day. No casualties, full reconciliation, and a media footprint of one paragraph. That's not luck, that's execution. Go home, and don't let anybody buy you a drink for it.
lines.coen: Then it was a good day. Nobody hurt. Everything counted. Tomorrow it's a paragraph nobody reads. That's about as good as it gets, in this line.

lines.current: First one. I moved when Snow said move and I did not make anything worse.
lines.why: A school report card. The kid sounds meek next to Snow and Lou. He should be trying to sound calm and failing.
lines.house: First one. I moved when Snow moved. I didn't make it worse. That's all I've got.
lines.tarantino: First one. I did what Snow said, when Snow said it, and I didn't make anything worse. I keep saying that in my head like it's an achievement. I don't know if it's an achievement.
lines.mcdonagh: First one. I moved when I was told and I made nothin' worse. That's the whole of me report, so it is.
lines.houser: First job. I followed Snow, I hit my marks, and I contributed nothing anybody will remember, which I'm told is the ideal outcome.
lines.coen: It was my first one. I moved when Snow said move. I didn't make anything worse. I don't know what else you want from me on that.

lines.current: We got out. Everybody came home.
lines.why: Mission-complete recap with no adrenaline in it after a shootout and a chase.
lines.house: We're out. Everybody's home. I can't feel my hands.
lines.tarantino: We got out. Everybody came home. And I'm sitting in a car outside my own building and I can't make myself open the door.
lines.mcdonagh: We got out. Everyone's home. And I've not stopped shakin' since the second car.
lines.houser: We're out, everybody's home, and I've just realised I'm still wearing the vest.
lines.coen: We got out. Everybody came home. That's — I keep saying that. I've said it about four times now.

lines.current: Buy the meat. Leave. No speeches.
lines.why: An on-screen objective in a mouth. It is also said twice, near-verbatim, later in the scene — which is what exposes it as tutorial text.
lines.house: You buy the meat, you get in the car. You don't make friends and you don't make a speech.
lines.tarantino: Here's the whole night. You buy the meat. You get in the car. Anything you say in between those two things is a mistake you haven't made yet.
lines.mcdonagh: Buy the meat. Get in the car. And whatever you're plannin' on sayin' — don't. I can see you plannin' it.
lines.houser: Transaction, then exit. No conversation, no negotiation, no personality. You're a wallet with legs tonight.
lines.coen: You buy the meat and then you leave. That's it. No speeches. People get hurt in the speeches.

lines.current: Buy. Leave. No speeches.
lines.why: The verbatim repeat. Fix by making the second one an escalation — he is saying it again because he can see the kid winding up.
lines.house: Buy. Leave. I said no speeches and I can see one on your face.
lines.tarantino: Buy. Leave. And I've now said it twice, which means I've seen something in you I don't like.
lines.mcdonagh: Buy. Leave. No speeches. That's twice. There'll not be a third, there'll just be me disappointed in a car.
lines.houser: Buy. Leave. And I'm repeating myself, which is a thing I do exactly once before I stop bringing somebody places.
lines.coen: Buy it. Leave. No speeches. I've said that now. I'd hate to have said it for nothing.

lines.current: Meat first. Money second. That is how this works.
lines.why: A rulebook line that Snow then parrots verbatim, making both men sound like the same laminated card. Rico should sound like he made this rule up because somebody once robbed him.
lines.house: Meat first, money second. That's not a rule, that's a scar.
lines.tarantino: Meat first. Money second. And before you tell me that's backwards — it is backwards. It's backwards on purpose, because the last man who did it the right way round is in a lake.
lines.mcdonagh: Meat first, money second. That's how it goes. Ask me why and I'll tell you about a fella in a lake.
lines.houser: Product first, payment second. Non-negotiable. I lost a lot of money learning that order and I'm not paying that tuition twice.
lines.coen: Meat first. Then the money. That's how we do it here. It's not how everybody does it. It's how we do it.

lines.current: Room twelve. Meat first. Money second.
lines.why: Snow repeating Rico's catchphrase back at him is the flattest kind of copy-paste. Snow should have his own read on the same rule, and it should be contemptuous.
lines.house: Room twelve. And he'll tell you meat first, money second, like it's scripture. Let him.
lines.tarantino: Room twelve. He's going to say meat first, money second, like he invented it. He didn't. Everybody says it. Let him have it.
lines.mcdonagh: Room twelve. He'll give you the meat-first-money-second speech. Nod along. He does love that speech.
lines.houser: Room twelve. He'll recite his little order-of-operations at you like it's a founding document. Let him finish, it's shorter that way.
lines.coen: Room twelve. He'll tell you meat first, money second. Just let him say it. He likes to say it.

lines.current: No, I am motel inspection.
lines.why: The cover story is the funniest idea in the scene and it is delivered like a stage direction. A bad lie has to be committed to, in detail, with paperwork energy.
lines.house: No. Motel inspection. County. I'm here about the ice machine and I'll be honest, I've heard things.
lines.tarantino: No. I'm motel inspection. County. And before you ask — no, I don't have a clipboard, because the county took the clipboards, which is its own scandal I'm not getting into with you in a doorway.
lines.mcdonagh: No. Motel inspection. And before you start — I know I don't look like it. Nobody looks like it. That's the whole point of it.
lines.houser: No. Motel inspection. County health, hospitality division. I'm here about the ice machine, the linens, and whatever is happening in your parking lot, which we'll get to.
lines.coen: No. I'm motel inspection. County. It's a — it's a real job. People are always surprised.

lines.current: I inspect standing.
lines.why: Reads like a translation error. The joke — he refuses to sit because sitting is how you get shot — is good and is not on the page.
lines.house: I'll stand. Inspectors stand. It's in the manual.
lines.tarantino: I'll stand, thanks. An inspector who sits down isn't inspecting, he's visiting. Different form entirely.
lines.mcdonagh: I'll stand. Inspectors stand. That's the difference between an inspection and a chat.
lines.houser: I'll remain standing. Seated inspections are a different form and a different fee, and neither of us wants that conversation.
lines.coen: I'll stand, if it's all the same. That's how it's done. Standing.

lines.current: That is how business works.
lines.why: A platitude any gangster in any film could say. It is also a line the kid has not earned yet.
lines.house: That's the deal. You don't have to like the deal.
lines.tarantino: That's business. And I know how that sounds coming out of me. I've been in this eleven weeks and I'm quoting people at you. But it's still true.
lines.mcdonagh: That's business. I'm told. I've only been at it a wet week, but that's what they keep sayin'.
lines.houser: That's the arrangement. I didn't write it, I just have to stand here in a bad room and enforce it.
lines.coen: That's how it works. I didn't come up with it. But that's how it works.

lines.current: Stand where I can see you.
lines.why: Generic guard-speak from a cartel lieutenant who should sound bored, southern, and completely certain he will win.
lines.house: Stand where I can see you. And take your hands out of that jacket before I take an interest.
lines.tarantino: Stand there. Right there, where the light is. I like to see a man's hands and I like to see his shoes, and I'll tell you why some other time.
lines.mcdonagh: Stand where I can see you. And keep your hands out of that coat, you're makin' me curious and I'm awful when I'm curious.
lines.houser: Stand there where the light is. Hands out of the jacket. This is a very simple room and I'd like to keep it that way.
lines.coen: Stand right there where I can see you. Hands out. It's easier for everybody.

lines.current: Not worth it, not worth it!
lines.why: Generic panic filler with none of Rico's personality. A man who has been swaggering all scene should break in his own specific way.
lines.house: It's not worth it — it's meat, it's just meat, take the meat!
lines.tarantino: It's not worth it. Look at me. Look at what we're doing. It's dried meat. We are all going to die in a motel over dried meat.
lines.mcdonagh: It's not worth it! It's jerky! We're all goin' to be shot over jerky and I'll not have that on me headstone!
lines.houser: It's not worth it! It's a commodity! It's a low-margin commodity and none of us are insured!
lines.coen: It's not worth it. It's really not. It's meat. It's just — it's meat, fellas.

lines.current: Yes.
lines.why: One of a whole family of one-word Prospect responses across the Beef Run that turn the player's mouth into a dialogue-menu confirm button. Fix the pattern, not just this line.
lines.house: Yeah. I see it.
lines.tarantino: Yeah. I'm looking right at it and I still don't believe it.
lines.mcdonagh: I do, aye. I wish I didn't, but I do.
lines.houser: Affirmative, and I'd like it noted I saw it and said nothing for a full ten seconds.
lines.coen: Yeah. Yeah, I see it. Huh.

lines.current: What exactly are we picking up?
lines.why: 'Exactly' is the tell — this is a quest prompt. Make the kid ask like someone who has already guessed and is hoping he is wrong.
lines.house: What are we actually picking up? And don't say meat.
lines.tarantino: So what are we picking up. And I want you to answer that without using the word meat, because every time somebody says meat in this outfit it turns out not to be meat.
lines.mcdonagh: What are we pickin' up? And don't say meat. Every time someone says meat I end up carryin' somethin' I'd rather not.
lines.houser: What is the actual cargo? And I'd appreciate the real answer, not the customs answer.
lines.coen: What are we picking up, exactly? I only ask because it's my name on the flight plan.

lines.current: Why is it illegal?
lines.why: Quest-log phrasing. He should be reacting, not requesting exposition.
lines.house: How is that illegal? It's a photograph.
lines.tarantino: Explain to me how a photograph is illegal. Not a gun. Not a body. A photograph.
lines.mcdonagh: How's a photo illegal? It's a photo. Of what? Of who?
lines.houser: It's a photograph. What jurisdiction on earth makes a photograph a felony, and how much are we getting paid for it?
lines.coen: Why would that be illegal? It's a picture. I don't — okay.

lines.current: I don't know how.
lines.why: Whiny and generic for a man flying contraband through a mountain range. His panic should be competent-adjacent.
lines.house: I don't know how to do that. Tell me how to do that. Tell me now.
lines.tarantino: I don't know how. Nobody showed me. There was a whole afternoon where somebody could have shown me and instead we talked about jerky.
lines.mcdonagh: I don't know how! Nobody showed me! We'd a full afternoon and we spent it talkin' about meat!
lines.houser: I don't know how. This was not in the onboarding, and I want you to sit with the fact that there was no onboarding.
lines.coen: I don't know how to do that. Nobody told me. That's not — I'm not being difficult, I just don't know how.

lines.current: Understood.
lines.why: Corporate. The kid is being lectured about jerky lineage by a man who takes it deadly seriously; his answer should show he has clocked that.
lines.house: Understood. I won't say the word again.
lines.tarantino: Understood. And I want you to know I will never say that word in this vehicle again as long as I live.
lines.mcdonagh: Understood. I'll never say it again. Not once. Not even in me head.
lines.houser: Understood. Noted. Internalized. I will die before I use that word incorrectly in front of you again.
lines.coen: Understood. I won't bring it up again. That's my mistake.

lines.current: Should I help?
lines.why: Deferential and small. He can offer without sounding like an intern.
lines.house: You want a hand, or is this a thing I'm not supposed to see?
lines.tarantino: You want a hand with that? Or is this one of those things where I help and then I know something.
lines.mcdonagh: D'you want a hand? Or am I better off lookin' at that tree for a bit?
lines.houser: Do you need help, or would helping make me a participant? Because I'm learning those are different.
lines.coen: You want a hand with that? I don't mind. I'd just as soon be useful.
